_comment: A small batch of Stage 4 bulk-classification outputs for ψυχή. Each record is the JSON object a single gpt-5.4-mini call emits, against the canonical inventory produced by Stage 3. Bulk classification is cheap and fast; the register/metre signal from Stage 1 is the main mechanism by which near-synonymous senses get disambiguated.

classifications.reason: Butler/Lattimore render as 'souls'; context 'Ἄιδι προΐαψεν' + epic register lock in the Homeric sense.
Il. 23.65 — Patroclus' ghost appears to Achilles; translation 'ghost of Patroclus' is decisive.
Apology 29e; Jowett renders 'soul' and context is Socratic moral self-care. Register 'philosophical' rules out the Homeric sense.
Antigone 559 — Antigone speaks of her ψυχή; tragic register allows either 'life' or 'soul, self'. Choosing 'soul, self' on textual grounds (character's moral self-reference) with a notable fallback.
Matt. 6.25 — context is food and drink; ψυχή glossed by English 'life' rather than 'soul'. Koine register tips the balance from 'soul, self' to 'life'.
Matt. 6.25 parallel with no aligned English translation and an empty Stage 1 context record; insufficient evidence to classify. Flagged for re-inspection.

observations: Three of six classifications hit confidence > 0.9 — these are the cleanest cases and would form training signal for downstream modelling.
Occurrence 158 (Antigone) illustrates the register-as-tiebreaker pattern the pipeline was designed to exploit.
Occurrence 210 shows the value of the 'uncertain' escape hatch: rather than force a bad label, Stage 4 records the refusal and flags the passage.
